SMART Guidelines are Standards-based, Machine-readable, Adaptive, Requirements-based and Testable recommended digital capabilities, health and data content aligned with normative recommendations (17).
SMART Guidelines are WHO’s approach to systematize and accelerate the consistent application of recommended, life-saving interventions in the digital age.

The five knowledge layers comprise: - **L1 Narrative:** enhanced clinical, public health guidelines and data recommendations - **L2 Operational:** digital adaptation kits (DAKs) - **L3 Machine readable:** machine-readable recommendations - **L4 Executable:** reference applications and services - **L5 Dynamic:** precision health model.

These layers inform developers how to translate recommendations into specifications and standards; technologists how to integrate recommendations into updatable digital systems; and countries how to localize, make interoperable, institutionalize and update digital systems consistent with evidence-based recommendations (17).

WHO’s SMART Guidelines approach** | Layer | Knowledge layers and associated products | Country implementation (Localization / Adaptation) | | --- | --- | --- | | **L1 Narrative** | Guideline and data recommendations: Enhanced guidelines | National policies, guidelines, data, and operational procedures | | **L2 Operational** | Semi-structured documentation of operational and functional requirements: Digital adaptation kits | Localized requirements | | **L3 Machine readable** | Structured, software-neutral, specifications, code, terminology and interoperability standards: Machine-readable recommendations | Localized machine-readable code and standards | | **L4 Executable** | Software that is able to execute static algorithms and interoperable digital components and deliver operational and functional requirements: Reference software | Localized static digital services and applications within a digital health enterprise | | **L5 Dynamic** | Executable dynamic algorithms that are trained and optimized with advanced analytics to achieve prioritize outcomes: Precision health models | Dynamic digital applications and services trained and optimized for prioritized local outcomes | *Source: WHO SMART guidelines: optimising country-level use of guideline recommendations in the digital age (Mehl et al., 2021) (18).*
